title: The first recorded refresh: the 2024–2025 vintages arrive
summary: All nine data domains and the USGS minerals were re-pulled together for the corpus's first recorded refresh. The World Bank's compilation has advanced most population, urbanisation and electricity-access series to 2025 and the GDP family to 2024: 1,324 observations are new vintages or first publications, 37 carry upstream revisions, and 2 were withdrawn. Every change resolves to its claim ID in the complete record.
notes: This entry pays the corpus's known vintage drift: economy, society, geography and military were last pulled in June 2026 and the other five domains in August. All nine were re-pulled in one act; four moved — economy, society, geography and resources.

Two observations were withdrawn upstream: Bosnia and Herzegovina's 2024 inflation (its 2023 observation stands again), and Jordan's trade-openness series, whose latest published year moved back from 2024 to 2007 — a large retreat of the series' published span, recorded here as it stands.
Governance, health, education, technology and military were re-pulled with zero value changes: their publishers have not moved since the prior pulls. Absence of change is recorded, not assumed.
The USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries remain the 2026 edition; no mineral production figure or world total moved.

Of the 37 upstream revisions, most are recomputation-scale (relative shifts below one part in a million); the largest are Ghana's 2024 trade openness and the 2024 CO2-per-capita figures for Togo and Georgia.
Two first-ever observations: trade openness for Fiji (2024) and Sao Tome and Principe (2025).
